\section{Per-system sensitivity}
\label{app:persys}

The limit Table~\ref{tab:persys} quotes for a system is that of its best
window, a bound pair appearing under its primary's name. A window inside the
attribution mask constrains nothing (\S\ref{sec:summary}) and cannot be a best
window: a double dagger marks a row keeping less than half its channels, and
\NSysALostName{}, whose \UmNWinALostWin{} windows are all inside it, is
tabulated with dashes. Beside each limit are that window's centre frequency
$\nu$ and channel width $\Delta\nu$, the system's merged coverage
$\Delta\nu_{\rm cov}$, the percentage \emph{dec.} by which atmospheric
decorrelation leaves the limit optimistic, and whether blocks of different
sessions cover a common frequency more than a day (d) or a year (yr) apart,
over the census and the \ZcNRecEB{} blocks the recurrence test reads. \emph{The decorrelation column is measured where the delivery allows
it and imputed where it does not}: an asterisk marks the
\NgNDecImpSys{} systems whose best window lies in a block with no phase record
of its own, imputed from the blocks matched to it in baseline, against
\NgNDecMeasSys{} measured, with a dash for the one system whose
blocks offer neither. The \NmDecSysMedPct{} per cent of
\S\ref{sec:pninetysel} is therefore a mixture: \NgDecMeasMedPct{} per cent
over the measured systems and \NgDecImpMedPct{} over the imputed, whose
estimate is a median over matched blocks and so has little spread of its own. Those blocks are not a random subset -- \NbDecPctTwelveUn{} per cent
12\,m against \NbDecPctTwelveMeas{} per cent of the ones that do expose a
record, that array's long baselines being what loses coherence -- so each of
their windows is matched to measured blocks within a factor of two in baseline
length: \RpDecMatchMed{} per cent in the median of those windows, and
\RpDecMatchHi{} per cent had each performed like the ninetieth-percentile
block matched to it, which is a condition on a calibration performance the
archive does not report. Every value in the column is a floor: the phase rms
is recorded on the calibrator, not on the target.
A dagger marks the \SmcNMeasSys{} of the \NSysALim{} systems whose own best
window was one of the \SensNInj{} injected into, so that their completeness is
measured; the other \SmcNEstSys{} limits are transferred from the class
average and carry instead
the dispersion observed between injected windows, $\times\SmcDispLo$ to
$\times\SmcDispHi$, and for the \NgNExtrapSys{} \NgExtrapSysNoun{} whose
best window lies outside the injected range in band, channel width, array
configuration or integration time that dispersion is itself transferred. Drawing each window's factor from the
\SensNInj{} measured ones instead, over \ScRsNTrial{} trials, shifts the
per-system median by \ScRsMedShiftPct{} per cent of the adopted
$\EirpNinetyMultA$, which is how far a minimum over estimates favours low
factors.
The full treatment is in \texttt{documentation/\allowbreak appendix\_F\_per\_system.md} of
the data archive \citep{SIdeposit}.
